1.description: Monarch butterflies clustered in dense overwintering groups on eucalyptus and Monterey pine trees along the central coast
1.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of orange butterflies hang together in trees like living curtains. When the sun warms them, they start to flutter!

1.description: Gray whales migrating southbound along the California coast toward Baja breeding lagoons, visible spouting from shore
1.childFriendlyNote: Watch the ocean for a puff of mist. That's a whale breathing! They're swimming all the way to Mexico to have their babies

1.description: Hillsides turning vivid green from winter rains, a carpet of new grass sprouting across coastal ranges
1.childFriendlyNote: The hills are turning bright green like a giant's lawn. The rain woke up all the sleeping seeds!

1.description: Male Anna's hummingbirds performing spectacular dive displays, flashing iridescent pink-red gorget in courtship
1.childFriendlyNote: A tiny bird zooms straight up into the sky, then dives back down with a loud squeak. He is showing off his sparkly pink throat.

1.description: Pacific tree frogs calling from rain-filled ponds and ditches, their loud 'ribbit' chorus carrying far on wet evenings
1.childFriendlyNote: After the rain, listen for a loud 'ribbit, ribbit'. These tiny green frogs are smaller than your thumb, and louder than a dog.

2.description: Monarch overwintering clusters still dense on coastal trees, butterflies basking on warm afternoons
2.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of orange butterflies hang together in trees like living curtains. When the sun warms them, they start to flutter!

2.description: Peak of southbound gray whale migration, watch for spouts and flukes from headlands and piers
2.childFriendlyNote: Watch the ocean for a puff of mist. That's a whale breathing! They're swimming all the way to Mexico to have their babies

2.description: Hillsides lush green from winter rains, new grass thick and soft across coastal valleys
2.childFriendlyNote: The hills are bright green like a giant's lawn. Run your hand through the soft new grass and smell the fresh earth

2.description: Anna's hummingbirds already nesting, females building tiny lichen-covered nests the size of a walnut
2.childFriendlyNote: A tiny bird zooms straight up into the sky, then dives back down with a loud squeak. She might already have eggs in a nest as small as a bottle cap.

2.description: Pacific tree frog chorus growing louder from rain pools and seasonal ponds
2.childFriendlyNote: After the rain, a huge 'ribbit, ribbit' chorus rises from every puddle. These frogs are smaller than your thumb, and every one of them is loud.

2.description: Acacia trees bursting into bright yellow pom-pom flowers, one of the first splashes of color in winter gardens
2.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow pom-pom flowers cover whole trees like golden clouds. Lean in close and smell the sweet honey scent

3.description: Monarch overwintering clusters still present, butterflies becoming more active on warm afternoons
3.childFriendlyNote: On sunny days, the butterflies wake up and float away from their cluster to sip nectar. Then they come back to cuddle at night!

3.description: Southbound gray whale migration continuing, mothers-to-be heading for warm lagoons
3.childFriendlyNote: Whales are still passing by. Look for their heart-shaped blow of mist from a cliff or pier

3.description: Acacia trees in full golden bloom along streets and in parks, fragrant on warm days
3.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy yellow pom-pom flowers cover whole trees like golden clouds. Lean in close and smell the sweet honey scent

3.description: Anna's hummingbirds actively nesting, males performing dramatic dive displays
3.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird dad flies way up high then dives down fast, making a loud chirp at the bottom. He's saying 'Look at me!'

3.description: California newts migrating to breeding ponds after winter rains, crossing trails and roads at night
3.childFriendlyNote: After rain, bumpy brown salamanders walk slowly across paths heading to ponds. They look like tiny dinosaurs! Don't touch though, their skin is yucky-tasting to keep predators away

3.description: Pacific tree frog breeding chorus at full volume from ponds and wet areas
3.childFriendlyNote: The frog choir is at its loudest now. Hundreds of tiny frogs all sing 'ribbit' together after dark.

4.description: Monarch clusters beginning to thin as butterflies start dispersing on warm days
4.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly sleepover is ending. More and more orange wings drift away from the trees each sunny day

4.description: Late southbound gray whales passing California, some early northbound mothers with new calves
4.childFriendlyNote: Some whales are heading south, but a few mums with brand new babies are already swimming back north. Look for a big blow and a tiny one next to it!

4.description: Acacia in full bloom, dropping golden pollen that dusts parked cars and sidewalks yellow
4.childFriendlyNote: The golden pom-pom trees shake yellow dust everywhere. Cars parked underneath get covered in yellow fairy dust!

4.description: California newts arriving at breeding ponds, males developing smooth skin and flattened tails for swimming
4.childFriendlyNote: The bumpy little newts are swimming in ponds now, doing a slow underwater dance to find a partner

4.description: Almond orchards exploding into pink-white bloom across the Central Valley, buzzing with honeybees
4.childFriendlyNote: Whole orchards turn pink and white, like snow made of flowers. Listen for the buzz of thousands of bees having a feast.

4.description: Hills at their greenest, winter rains keeping grasslands lush and emerald
4.childFriendlyNote: The hills are the greenest green you've ever seen, like someone colored them with the brightest crayon in the box!

5.description: Almond blossoms at peak across the Central Valley, a sea of pink and white petals
5.childFriendlyNote: Rows and rows of trees covered in pink flowers stretch as far as you can see. It looks like a fairy kingdom!

5.description: Southbound migration tapering off, first northbound mothers and calves appearing
5.childFriendlyNote: The whale parade is slowing down, but keep watching! Some mums with new babies are heading back north already

5.description: Newts breeding in ponds, laying eggs on submerged vegetation
5.childFriendlyNote: Peek into a pond and you might see newts doing their slow underwater dance. They lay tiny jelly eggs on underwater plants

5.description: Anna's hummingbird chicks hatching in walnut-sized nests, females feeding constantly
5.childFriendlyNote: Baby hummingbirds are hatching. They're the size of a jellybean! Mum feeds them by poking her long beak into their tiny mouths

5.description: Hills at peak green, lush from steady winter rains
5.childFriendlyNote: The hills look like a green velvet blanket. They smell fresh and alive after every rain shower

5.description: Manzanita shrubs covered in clusters of tiny pink-white urn-shaped flowers, buzzing with native bees
5.childFriendlyNote: Smooth red-barked bushes are covered in tiny pink bells. Lean close and hear the buzz of hungry bees visiting every flower

6.description: Almond blossoms fading, petals drifting down like snow in Central Valley orchards
6.childFriendlyNote: Pink petals are raining down from the almond trees. Walk underneath and feel them land softly on your head!

6.description: Manzanita in full bloom, smooth reddish bark and clusters of tiny bell flowers attracting early pollinators
6.childFriendlyNote: Feel the smooth, cool bark of the manzanita. It feels like a polished stone. The tiny bells on top buzz with bees!

6.description: Acorn woodpeckers chattering loudly from granary trees, maintaining their acorn stash holes from last autumn
6.childFriendlyNote: Clown-faced birds with red caps laugh 'waka-waka' from trees full of holes. Each hole has an acorn stuffed in it, like a little pantry.

6.description: Tree frog chorus at peak volume, egg masses visible in shallow ponds
6.childFriendlyNote: The frog concert is the loudest it'll be all year. Look in the water for blobs of clear jelly with tiny black dots inside. Those are frog eggs!

6.description: Anna's hummingbirds feeding on winter-blooming sage and rosemary
6.childFriendlyNote: The tiny sparkly hummingbird zips from flower to flower so fast your eyes can barely follow. Its wings beat 50 times a second!

6.description: Hillsides vividly green, winter rains keeping grasslands lush and growing
6.childFriendlyNote: Every hill looks like it was painted green overnight. The rain is magic paint for the Earth!

7.description: Manzanita bloom fading, tiny bell flowers dropping and small green berries forming
7.childFriendlyNote: The tiny pink bells are falling off the smooth red bushes, and baby green berries are starting to grow in their place

7.description: First California poppy leaves appearing in sunny grasslands, ferny blue-green foliage spreading low
7.childFriendlyNote: Feathery blue-green leaves are spreading on the ground like little ferns. They're getting ready to become California's famous orange flowers!

7.description: Acorn woodpeckers vocal and active, beginning to prepare nesting cavities in oaks
7.childFriendlyNote: The clown-faced birds are hammering new holes in the trees, tap tap tap, getting their house ready for babies.

7.description: Emerald green hillsides at their most vibrant, with early wildflower rosettes starting to form
7.childFriendlyNote: The hills are so green they almost glow. Look closely at the ground and you will see tiny baby wildflowers getting ready.

7.description: Newts still breeding in ponds, egg masses visible on submerged branches
7.childFriendlyNote: Look in ponds for brownish salamanders swimming slowly. They've wrapped their jelly eggs around twigs underwater

7.description: Wild lilac buds swelling on hillside shrubs, getting ready to bloom
7.childFriendlyNote: Bushes on the hillsides are covered in tiny tight buds. Soon they'll explode into clouds of blue and purple flowers!

8.description: First California poppy buds appearing, pointed caps ready to pop off and reveal orange petals
8.childFriendlyNote: The poppy buds wear pointy green hats. When they're ready, the hat pops right off and out comes a crinkly orange flower!

8.description: Wild lilac shrubs beginning to bloom, first blue-purple flower clusters opening on sunny slopes
8.childFriendlyNote: The hillside bushes are opening their first blue flowers. Lean in and sniff, they smell sweet like honey mixed with vanilla!

8.description: Hills at peak green with early wildflower patches starting to dot the landscape
8.childFriendlyNote: The green hills are getting sprinkled with tiny flower dots. Nature is decorating!

8.description: Allen's hummingbirds arriving back from Mexico, males performing pendulum courtship flights
8.childFriendlyNote: A new hummingbird is back from vacation! He swings back and forth in the air like he's on an invisible swing

8.description: Tree frogs still chorusing loudly, tadpoles hatching in ponds
8.childFriendlyNote: The frogs are still singing their hearts out, and their eggs have hatched too. Look for tiny wiggly tadpoles in the pond.

8.description: Acorn woodpeckers nesting in communal cavities, whole family group helping
8.childFriendlyNote: The whole woodpecker family works together. Grandma, uncle, everyone helps feed the babies. They're the best team in the forest!

9.description: California poppies opening in warm spots, bright orange blooms closing at night and on cloudy days
9.childFriendlyNote: The first orange poppies are open! They close up tight at night like little sleeping bags. Come back in the morning to see them open again

9.description: Wild lilac blooming across hillsides, filling the air with sweet fragrance
9.childFriendlyNote: Whole hillsides are covered in fluffy blue-purple flowers that smell amazing. Close your eyes and breathe in!

9.description: Hills still brilliantly green with wildflower season beginning to paint the grasslands
9.childFriendlyNote: Green hills are getting their first splashes of orange and purple. It's like nature is starting a painting!

9.description: First barn swallows returning from Central America, swooping over fields catching insects
9.childFriendlyNote: Speedy birds with forked tails are back from their winter holiday. They swoop and dive catching tiny bugs in midair like little acrobats!

9.description: Lupine leaves spreading across grasslands, their distinctive fan-shaped foliage carpeting meadows
9.childFriendlyNote: Look for leaves shaped like tiny green hands reaching up from the grass. They'll grow tall purple flower spikes soon!

10.description: California poppies spreading rapidly across hillsides and roadsides, orange blooms multiplying daily
10.childFriendlyNote: More and more orange poppies pop open every day. Soon whole hillsides will look like they're on fire with color!

10.description: Wild lilac at peak bloom, hillsides fragrant with blue-purple flower clouds buzzing with bees
10.childFriendlyNote: The wild lilac smells sweet, and the bees think so too. Whole hillsides are blue-purple and buzzing.

10.description: Lupine flower spikes emerging, purple and blue towers rising from fan-shaped leaves
10.childFriendlyNote: Purple towers are popping up in the meadow. Each one is covered in tiny flowers shaped like little butterflies!

10.description: Barn swallows arriving in greater numbers, beginning to scout nesting sites under eaves and bridges
10.childFriendlyNote: The fork-tailed swallows are house-hunting! Watch them zoom under bridges and porches looking for the perfect spot to build a mud nest

10.description: Hillsides still lush green with wildflowers beginning to create colorful patches
10.childFriendlyNote: The green hills are getting dressed up with orange poppies and purple lupines, nature's spring fashion show!

10.description: Western fence lizards emerging from winter dormancy, basking on rocks and fence posts in morning sun
10.childFriendlyNote: Little grey lizards are sunbathing on rocks and fences. They do tiny push-ups to show off their bright blue bellies!

11.description: California poppies blooming strongly, whole hillsides beginning to glow orange
11.childFriendlyNote: Hillsides are turning orange with poppies! They open wide in sunshine and wrap up tight when clouds come, like they have their own weather app

11.description: Lupine spikes blooming in meadows and along roadsides, purple mixed with orange poppies
11.childFriendlyNote: Purple and orange wildflowers are painting the meadows like an artist went wild with their favorite colors!

11.description: Wild lilac bloom still strong on hillsides, fragrance carrying on warm breezes
11.childFriendlyNote: Take a deep breath on a hillside walk. That sweet perfume is wild lilac, and it's everywhere!

11.description: Fence lizards doing push-up displays on walls and rocks, males flashing blue belly patches
11.childFriendlyNote: The lizards are doing push-ups on every fence post. They bob up and down to say 'this is my rock'. Can you do push-ups too?

11.description: Barn swallows building mud nests under eaves, gathering mouthfuls of wet mud from puddles
11.childFriendlyNote: Watch swallows scoop up mud from puddles and fly it to their nest. They build their house one tiny mud ball at a time!

11.description: Northbound gray whale migration picking up, mothers swimming close to shore with calves
11.childFriendlyNote: Whale mums are swimming north with their babies right along the coast. The babies are already as big as a car!

12.description: California poppies at spectacular peak, hillsides blazing orange in the warm late-March sunshine
12.childFriendlyNote: The hillsides look like they caught fire with the most beautiful orange flames, but they're flowers! Lie down in a poppy field and look up at the sky

12.description: Lupines blooming thickly in meadows, creating purple carpets mixed with orange poppies, the classic California wildflower display
12.childFriendlyNote: Purple and orange flowers cover the meadow like a patchwork quilt made by a giant. It smells sweet and the bees are humming!

12.description: Hills still vibrantly green beneath the wildflower show, the last weeks of peak green before summer gold begins
12.childFriendlyNote: The hills are still bright green, and now they are covered in wildflowers too. This is California's most magical time of year.

12.description: Northbound gray whale migration in full swing, cow-calf pairs hugging the coastline
12.childFriendlyNote: Whale mums and their babies are swimming past right now. Grab binoculars and look for their misty breath puffs from any high spot near the ocean!

12.description: Fence lizards very active, males doing vigorous push-up displays and chasing rivals from sunny perches
12.childFriendlyNote: Every sunny wall has a tiny lizard doing push-ups like a gym instructor, up down, up down, flashing its blue tummy.

12.description: Cliff swallows returning to nesting colonies, traditionally arriving at Mission San Juan Capistrano around March 19
12.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are back! Every year they fly thousands of miles from South America to build their mud nests in the same spot, like coming home from the longest trip ever!

13.description: California poppies at full peak, blazing orange across entire landscapes in the Antelope Valley and coastal hills
13.childFriendlyNote: Fields of orange stretch as far as you can see. It looks like the ground is glowing! These are California's state flower and this is their big moment

13.description: Lupines at peak alongside poppies, the purple and orange superbloom display at its best
13.childFriendlyNote: Purple and orange flowers are having a competition to see who can cover more ground. It's a tie and everyone wins!

13.description: Cliff swallows busy building gourd-shaped mud nests under bridges and building eaves
13.childFriendlyNote: The swallows are building nests shaped like little mud igloos under bridges. They carry mud in their beaks, one tiny ball at a time!

13.description: Peak of northbound gray whale migration, mothers and calves passing close to shore
13.childFriendlyNote: The whale parade is at its busiest. Mums teach their babies to swim by staying in the shallow water near the beach

13.description: Fence lizards in peak breeding activity, males territorial and displaying constantly
13.childFriendlyNote: The push-up lizards are working overtime. They bob so fast it looks like they're dancing on the fence!

13.description: Painted lady butterflies beginning spring migration northward through California in some years
13.childFriendlyNote: Orange and brown butterflies flutter past in groups. They are on a long trip from Mexico, all the way to Oregon and beyond.

14.description: Poppies blooming prolifically across hillsides and road verges, peak wildflower season in full swing
14.childFriendlyNote: Orange poppies are everywhere: along roads, on hills, in gardens. They close up every night and open fresh each morning.

14.description: Lupines in full bloom, purple spikes thick in coastal grasslands and inland valleys
14.childFriendlyNote: Purple flower towers stand proud in the fields. Each little flower on the spike looks like a tiny butterfly resting

14.description: Owl's clover adding pink-purple splashes to wildflower meadows among the poppies and lupines
14.childFriendlyNote: Pink fuzzy flowers dot the meadow between the orange and purple ones. The wildflower show has all the colors in it.

14.description: Cliff swallow colonies busy, birds swooping to catch insects and carrying mud to growing nests
14.childFriendlyNote: Under the bridge, mud igloos are getting bigger every day. The swallows work from sunrise to sunset!

14.description: Painted ladies migrating through in growing numbers, nectaring on wildflowers
14.childFriendlyNote: Butterflies are streaming through like a sky river. Sometimes millions pass through California in a single spring!

14.description: Hills still green but beginning to show first hints of gold on south-facing slopes
14.childFriendlyNote: The green hills are still going strong but look closely: a few sunny slopes are starting to turn gold at the tips, like nature's highlighter

15.description: California poppies still blooming strongly, peak shifting to higher elevations and northern areas
15.childFriendlyNote: The orange poppies are still showing off. Touch the silky petals gently, they feel like the softest tissue paper

15.description: Lupines in full bloom, some early flowers fading and forming seed pods
15.childFriendlyNote: The purple towers are starting to make seeds at the bottom while still flowering at the top, busy multitaskers!

15.description: Lesser goldfinches in bright breeding plumage singing from treetops and feeding on thistle seeds
15.childFriendlyNote: Tiny bright yellow birds bounce through the air like flying tennis balls, singing a cheerful twittering song from every tree!

15.description: Fence lizards very active, females developing eggs, males still displaying from prominent perches
15.childFriendlyNote: The lizards are everywhere now. Freeze and watch one, it'll stare right back at you with its beady eyes and do a push-up!

15.description: California quail pairs nesting in dense shrubs, males calling 'chi-ca-go' from fence posts as sentinels
15.childFriendlyNote: A plump bird with a funny curly feather on its head calls 'chi-ca-go, chi-ca-go' from a fence. He is the lookout while his family hides in the bushes.

16.description: Poppies still blooming but beginning to slow in low-elevation areas as the soil dries
16.childFriendlyNote: The poppies are still glowing orange. Watch a bumblebee crawl inside one and come out covered in golden pollen dust!

16.description: California quail incubating eggs in hidden ground nests, males on lookout duty
16.childFriendlyNote: The quail dad stands guard on a high spot calling 'chi-ca-go' while mum sits quietly on her eggs, hidden in the grass.

16.description: Lesser goldfinches singing constantly, pairs building tiny cup nests in trees
16.childFriendlyNote: Little yellow birds sing a bubbly song while weaving the tiniest nest you've ever seen, smaller than a teacup!

16.description: Hills starting their transition from green to gold, south-facing slopes drying first as spring rains diminish
16.childFriendlyNote: The green hills are starting to get golden streaks, like nature is slowly painting them with a gold crayon from the bottom up

16.description: California buckeye trees in full fresh leaf, large palmate leaves creating dense canopy
16.childFriendlyNote: A tree with big hand-shaped leaves is showing off its best green outfit. Each leaf looks like a spread-out hand waving at you!

16.description: Painted lady migration continuing, sometimes in spectacular numbers across hillsides
16.childFriendlyNote: Orange butterflies float through the air in groups. They're on the longest trip of their lives, flying all the way to Oregon!

17.description: Poppies fading at lower elevations, still blooming at higher spots and along the coast
17.childFriendlyNote: Some poppies are making seed pods now. They look like long skinny green fingers. Shake a dry one and hear tiny seeds rattle inside!

17.description: California buckeye producing tall white-pink flower spikes, fragrant and buzzing with bees and butterflies
17.childFriendlyNote: The hand-leaf tree is putting on candle-shaped flowers, white and pink towers that smell sweet and are covered in busy bees!

17.description: Hills increasingly golden-brown, the famous California gold spreading as grasses dry and set seed
17.childFriendlyNote: The green is fading to gold like magic. California's hills are putting on their summer outfit!

17.description: Barn swallows incubating eggs in mud cup nests, swooping constantly to catch flying insects
17.childFriendlyNote: Parent swallows zoom back and forth catching bugs. They have babies to feed soon and need lots of food!

17.description: First quail chicks hatching, tiny cotton-ball-sized babies running after parents in a line
17.childFriendlyNote: Tiny quail babies the size of cotton balls run after their mum in a wobbly line. Count them, there might be 10 or more!

17.description: Lupines setting seed at lower elevations, rattly pods developing, still blooming in cooler spots
17.childFriendlyNote: The purple flowers are turning into fuzzy pea pods. When they dry out in the sun, they pop open and fling their seeds.

18.description: Buckeye flower spikes at peak, tall white candles visible across woodland hillsides
18.childFriendlyNote: White flower candles glow on the trees. Some of them are longer than your arm.

18.description: Hillsides rapidly turning from green to golden as spring rains end and summer drought begins
18.childFriendlyNote: The golden color is spreading fast across the hills. Soon they'll look like they're made of honey!

18.description: Quail family groups visible, tiny striped chicks scurrying after parents through garden edges
18.childFriendlyNote: A line of tiny striped quail babies follows mum like a little train. They can run almost as fast as you on their teeny legs!

18.description: Brown pelicans nesting on offshore islands, adults spectacular with red-brown neck plumage
18.childFriendlyNote: Big pelicans with pouchy beaks fly in a line over the waves, like a squadron of prehistoric birds. Then, splash, they dive headfirst for fish.

18.description: Foxtail grass going to seed in grasslands and along paths, bristly seed heads catching on socks and pet fur
18.childFriendlyNote: Fuzzy grass seeds shaped like fox tails stick to everything: your socks, your shoelaces, your dog! They're nature's hitchhikers

18.description: Barn swallow chicks hatching, parents making constant feeding trips with beakfuls of insects
18.childFriendlyNote: Baby swallows open their bright yellow mouths wide and cheep cheep when mum and dad bring bugs. They are always hungry.

19.description: Buckeye flowers fading, early leaves beginning to brown as the tree prepares for summer dormancy
19.childFriendlyNote: The buckeye tree is already getting sleepy for summer. Its leaves are turning brown while other trees are still green. It naps through the hot months!

19.description: Hills mostly golden-brown now, the iconic California summer landscape establishing
19.childFriendlyNote: The hills have turned into golden waves. This is what makes California look like California in the movies!

19.description: Foxtail grass seed heads drying and sharp, easily catching in clothing and pet fur
19.childFriendlyNote: Pick a foxtail and brush it on your arm. Feel how it only goes one way? That's how it burrows into the ground to plant itself!

19.description: Brown pelicans feeding actively along the coast, spectacular plunge-diving into schools of fish
19.childFriendlyNote: Watch the pelicans fold up their wings and crash into the water beak-first. Their throat pouch fills with water and fish, like a fishing net.

19.description: Fence lizards laying eggs in warm soil, males still doing push-up territory displays
19.childFriendlyNote: The push-up lizards are still going strong. Lady lizards have buried their eggs in warm sandy soil to cook in the sun

20.description: Golden hills now the dominant landscape, dried grass seeds scattering in warm breezes
20.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills whisper and rustle in the wind. Run your hand through the dry grass and listen to it crackle

20.description: Buckeye leaves dropping rapidly, trees going dormant months before other deciduous trees
20.childFriendlyNote: This tree is losing its leaves in May. While everything else is green, the buckeye is going to sleep to save water. Smart tree.

20.description: Brown pelicans in full breeding season, spectacular diving displays along the coast
20.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans circle high above the waves, then tuck and dive. Splash. They catch fish in their big stretchy beak pouch.

20.description: Barn swallow chicks growing fast, parents exhausted from constant insect-catching runs
20.childFriendlyNote: The baby swallows are getting big and fluffy. They peer over the edge of the mud nest and chirp for more food.

20.description: Quail families with growing chicks foraging together, multiple broods sometimes merging into large groups
20.childFriendlyNote: Quail kindergarten! Sometimes two families join together so 20 babies all run around in one big group. It's quail daycare!

20.description: Foxtail seeds at their sharpest, care needed on walks as they penetrate socks and animal ears
20.childFriendlyNote: Watch out for foxtails on your socks! These sneaky seeds have tiny barbs that only go one direction. Check your shoes after a walk

21.description: Hills fully golden-brown, dry summer pattern well established across California
21.childFriendlyNote: Golden hills stretch in every direction. They glow warm amber in the late afternoon sun

21.description: Brown pelicans feeding chicks on nesting islands, adults commuting to fishing grounds
21.childFriendlyNote: Pelican mums and dads fly out to sea to fill their beaks with fish, then fly back to feed their fluffy grey babies

21.description: Fence lizards basking in early morning before retreating from midday heat
21.childFriendlyNote: The lizards are early birds now. They sunbathe in the cool morning then hide in the shade when it gets too hot. They're sun-smart!

21.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring over golden hills on thermals, hunting ground squirrels in open grasslands
21.childFriendlyNote: A big hawk circles slowly over the golden hills without even flapping. Listen for a long 'keeeeer'. That screaming call means 'this is my sky'.

21.description: Ground squirrels very active, standing upright as sentinels and chirping alarm calls at passersby
21.childFriendlyNote: Chubby squirrels stand up tall on their back legs like meerkats and chirp warnings to each other. One sees you and the whole family dives underground!

22.description: Hills deep golden, dried grass stems crackling underfoot in the warming weather
22.childFriendlyNote: Walk through the golden grass and listen to it crunch. Each step sounds like nature's Rice Krispies.

22.description: Brown pelicans flying in V-formations along the coast, diving spectacularly for sardines and anchovies
22.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans fly in a perfect line right above the waves. Then one by one they peel off and splash dive for fish.

22.description: Red-tailed hawk fledglings learning to fly, wobbly first flights from nest trees
22.childFriendlyNote: Baby hawks are trying their first flights. They wobble and flap clumsily, but soon they'll soar as well as their parents!

22.description: Ground squirrel pups emerging from burrows for the first time, curious and playful
22.childFriendlyNote: Tiny baby squirrels peek out of holes in the ground for the first time. They chase each other and tumble like furry puppies!

22.description: Marine layer fog rolling in from the Pacific, blanketing the coast in cool grey mist while inland valleys bake
22.childFriendlyNote: A thick cloud sits right on top of the ocean and creeps over the land. Walk through it and feel the cool, damp air on your face like a giant's breath!

23.description: June gloom, thick marine layer fog covering the coast each morning, burning off by afternoon inland
23.childFriendlyNote: June Gloom! A fluffy fog blanket covers the beach every morning. By lunchtime the sun burns through and it's warm again

23.description: Golden-brown hills fully established, dry grass seeds rattling in afternoon breezes
23.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills glow like honey in the warm sunshine. California's summer colors are here!

23.description: Ground squirrel families active in early morning and late evening, avoiding midday heat
23.childFriendlyNote: The squirrels are morning people now, they play and eat when it's cool, then disappear underground when the sun gets hot

23.description: First brood of barn swallows fledging, young birds practicing flying near the nest
23.childFriendlyNote: Young swallows take their first flights from the nest. They're a bit wobbly at first but soon they're zooming like their parents!

23.description: Red-tailed hawks riding thermals over golden hills, young hawks getting stronger on the wing
23.childFriendlyNote: Hawks ride invisible escalators of warm air up into the sky. They can see a mouse in the grass from way up high!

23.description: Tarweed plants beginning to bloom in dry grasslands, sticky yellow flowers that open in late afternoon
23.childFriendlyNote: Sticky yellow flowers pop open in the dry grass. Touch the stem and your fingers get gummy! They smell like warm tar on a road

24.description: June gloom marine layer persistent, fog dripping from trees in coastal areas providing summer moisture
24.childFriendlyNote: The fog is so thick that trees drip water even though it hasn't rained. Redwood trees drink fog like a giant straw!

24.description: Tarweed blooming in dry grasslands, one of the few wildflowers thriving in summer heat
24.childFriendlyNote: While everything else is dry and brown, sticky yellow tarweed flowers bloom bravely. They're the summer wildflower champions!

24.description: Brown pelicans fishing actively along beaches, young birds making clumsy practice dives
24.childFriendlyNote: Young pelicans are learning to fish. Their first dives are big belly-flops! But they get better every day

24.description: Ground squirrels foraging in early morning, some adults beginning summer estivation in hottest areas
24.childFriendlyNote: Some squirrels are so hot they take a summer nap underground. It's like hibernation but for heat instead of cold!

24.description: Fence lizards active in mornings and late afternoons, hatchlings starting to appear
24.childFriendlyNote: Teeny tiny baby lizards are hatching. They're barely as long as your finger and they can already do push-ups!

25.description: Marine layer fog still blanketing the coast most mornings, keeping coastal temperatures cool
25.childFriendlyNote: The fog is like nature's air conditioning for the beach. While inland is hot, the coast stays cool and misty

25.description: Golden-brown hills baking in summer heat, dried grass creating fire-danger conditions
25.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills are hot now. The dry grass is so crunchy you can hear it from far away when the wind blows.

25.description: Red-tailed hawks hunting over dry grasslands, young hawks now independent and learning to hunt alone
25.childFriendlyNote: Young hawks are hunting on their own now. Watch them hover in the wind then drop like a stone to catch a gopher!

25.description: Tarweed in full bloom across dry grasslands, sticky stems trapping small insects
25.childFriendlyNote: The tarweed flowers are so sticky that tiny bugs get trapped on the stems. It's almost like a carnivorous plant!

25.description: Quail families foraging in shady areas during heat, chicks now half-grown with developing topknots
25.childFriendlyNote: The quail teenagers are growing their own little curly head feathers. They stick up like a tiny question mark!

26.description: Deep golden-brown hills in the long dry season, thistles and dry seed heads the only upright plants
26.childFriendlyNote: The hills look like they're made of straw, but seeds are hiding in the soil, waiting patiently for rain

26.description: Brown pelicans fishing in large groups, young birds joining adults in coastal feeding
26.childFriendlyNote: A whole flock of pelicans dive-bombs the ocean at once, splash, splash, splash. It is a pelican pool party.

26.description: Ground squirrels most active at dawn, young of the year nearly full-sized
26.childFriendlyNote: The baby squirrels have grown up fast. They're almost as big as their parents and getting bold enough to come near people

26.description: Fence lizards everywhere, juveniles and adults basking and hunting insects on warm surfaces
26.childFriendlyNote: Lizards are on every wall and fence, snapping up ants and flies. They're the best pest control in your garden!

26.description: Tarweed still flowering bravely in parched grasslands, fragrant on hot afternoons
26.childFriendlyNote: Tough little yellow flowers keep blooming even when everything else has given up. They're the last ones standing in the dry grass

27.description: Deep summer golden hills, fire danger elevated across the state
27.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills shimmer in the heat. Everything is waiting for rain that won't come for months

27.description: Brown pelicans fishing along the coast, juveniles with brown heads now common
27.childFriendlyNote: Young pelicans have plain brown heads while the grown-ups have fancy white heads. Can you tell which is which?

27.description: Ground squirrels foraging mostly at dawn and dusk, staying underground during peak heat
27.childFriendlyNote: Even the squirrels think it's too hot. They only come out when the sun is low and spend the hot part of the day in their cool underground tunnels

27.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring on powerful summer thermals, hunting dry grasslands for ground squirrels
27.childFriendlyNote: Hawks love hot days. Warm air pushes them up high without even flapping. They surf the invisible sky waves!

27.description: Large green darner dragonflies patrolling ponds and streams, catching mosquitoes on the wing
27.childFriendlyNote: Huge green dragonflies zoom over the water like tiny helicopters. They can fly forwards, backwards, and even hover in place!

28.description: Peak of golden-brown summer hills, landscape at its most arid and warm-toned
28.childFriendlyNote: The hills are deep gold like a lion's mane. California looks like a wild savanna in summer

28.description: Pelicans gliding in long lines just above the wave crests, using updraft from waves
28.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans surf the air right above the waves without even flapping. They glide like feathered surfboards!

28.description: Dragonflies abundant over ponds and gardens, brilliant blue-green bodies catching the light
28.childFriendlyNote: Shimmering green dragonflies zip and hover over the water. Their wings are like tiny stained-glass windows in the sun!

28.description: Fence lizards avoiding midday heat, most active in mornings when surfaces are warm but not scorching
28.childFriendlyNote: Even the sun-loving lizards hide from the afternoon blaze. Catch them doing their push-ups early in the morning!

28.description: Large quail coveys gathering at water sources in early morning, chicks now nearly adult-sized
28.childFriendlyNote: Quail families gather at birdbaths and puddles to drink. It's the watering hole and everybody's invited!

28.description: Marine layer fog still common on the coast, burning off to sunny afternoons
28.childFriendlyNote: Mornings at the beach start grey and cool. Then the sun wins the battle and pushes the fog back out to sea!

29.description: Golden-brown hills at midsummer, fire weather conditions requiring vigilance
29.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills crackle in the heat. Everything is dry and waiting. This is why we're extra careful about fire in summer

29.description: Pelicans fishing in large flocks, sometimes hundreds gathering where fish are schooling near shore
29.childFriendlyNote: A huge flock of pelicans found the fish! They all dive at once. It's like watching the world's biggest belly-flop competition

29.description: Red-tailed hawks riding strong thermals, hunting from soaring height over dry grasslands
29.childFriendlyNote: Hawks circle higher and higher on the hot rising air. They can see the whole valley from up there!

29.description: Dragonflies patrolling gardens and ponds, catching countless mosquitoes and gnats
29.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies are like tiny fighter jets catching bugs in midair. One dragonfly eats hundreds of mosquitoes every day!

29.description: Ground squirrels using their bushy tails as sunshades, flipping them over their backs in the heat
29.childFriendlyNote: Ground squirrels hold their fluffy tails over their heads like tiny umbrellas to shade themselves from the hot sun, clever!

30.description: Golden-brown hills at peak summer, landscape at maximum dryness
30.childFriendlyNote: The hills are deep, toasty gold, like giant golden pancakes stretching to the horizon

30.description: Dragonflies abundant, laying eggs on pond vegetation, nymphs active underwater
30.childFriendlyNote: Dragonflies dip their tails into the water. They're laying eggs! The babies live underwater for a whole year before they fly

30.description: Pelicans active along every stretch of coast, a constant presence in the summer seascape
30.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans are everywhere at the beach. Watch them tuck their beaks into their chests and rest on the pier posts like sleepy old men

30.description: Scrub-jays caching food for autumn, boldly visiting gardens and picnic areas
30.childFriendlyNote: A bright blue bird with a loud shriek steals your sandwich crumbs. Scrub-jays are cheeky and smart. They hide food for later and remember every hiding spot.

30.description: Tarweed still flowering, yellow blooms in otherwise completely brown grasslands
30.childFriendlyNote: The last brave yellow flowers still bloom in the brown grass. The tarweed refuses to give up until every last bee has visited!

31.description: Hills remain golden-brown, August heat baking the landscape dry
31.childFriendlyNote: The hills are still made of gold. They've been this color for so long it feels like they were always this way

31.description: Perseid meteor shower begins, best viewed from dark locations away from city lights in warm summer evenings
31.childFriendlyNote: Shooting stars! Lie on a blanket outside after dark and count the streaks of light across the sky. Make a wish on each one!

31.description: Brown pelicans ranging widely along the coast, post-breeding dispersal beginning
31.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans are exploring the whole coast now. Big groups glide past in long wavy lines just above the waves

31.description: Scrub-jays busy caching acorns and seeds, their remarkable memory storing thousands of hiding spots
31.childFriendlyNote: The blue jay is burying acorns everywhere. It remembers thousands of hiding spots! The ones it forgets grow into new oak trees

31.description: Ground squirrels foraging intensely in mornings, building fat reserves for autumn estivation
31.childFriendlyNote: The squirrels are eating as much as they can. Like stocking up the pantry before a long nap!

32.description: Perseid meteor shower at peak, up to 100 shooting stars per hour visible on clear dark nights
32.childFriendlyNote: Tonight is the best night for shooting stars. Every few minutes a bright streak zips across the sky. They are really tiny space rocks burning up.

32.description: Golden-brown hills in deep summer, hot dry winds sometimes whipping across the landscape
32.childFriendlyNote: Hot wind makes the golden grass dance and wave. It looks like a golden ocean with waves rolling across the hills

32.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring in hot thermals, juveniles now fully independent hunters
32.childFriendlyNote: Young hawks are expert hunters now. They soar all by themselves, screaming their battle cry across the golden hills

32.description: Scrub-jays molting into fresh feathers, looking scruffy while new plumage grows in
32.childFriendlyNote: The blue jays look a bit messy right now. They're growing new feathers! Imagine changing all your clothes at the same time

32.description: Dragonflies still abundant, some beginning early southbound migration
32.childFriendlyNote: Did you know dragonflies migrate like birds? Some of these shiny green flyers will travel hundreds of miles south!

33.description: Perseid meteor shower fading but still producing occasional bright fireballs
33.childFriendlyNote: A few more shooting stars still streak across the sky, the leftover sparklers from the big space show

33.description: Hills at their most golden-brown, late summer heat and bone-dry conditions
33.childFriendlyNote: The hills are the deepest gold of the whole year, like honey and butter and sunshine all mixed together

33.description: Brown pelicans dispersing from breeding colonies, large numbers visible along the entire coast
33.childFriendlyNote: Pelicans are everywhere along the beach now. Count how many you can see in one glance!

33.description: Some adult ground squirrels entering estivation in hottest inland areas, juveniles still active
33.childFriendlyNote: The grown-up squirrels are disappearing underground for a summer snooze, but the young ones are still running around having fun!

33.description: Young fence lizards abundant, darting across paths and up fence posts
33.childFriendlyNote: Baby lizards are everywhere. They zip across the path so fast they look like little grey rockets!

33.description: Valley oak acorns developing on branches, still green and growing through the summer heat
33.childFriendlyNote: Look up in the oak tree. Green baby acorns are growing in their little cups, getting bigger and fatter every week

34.description: Golden-brown hills in late August, some south-facing slopes nearly white from sun bleaching
34.childFriendlyNote: Some hills are so dry they're almost white. The sun has bleached the grass like old bones in the desert

34.description: Valley oak acorns getting larger, starting to show brown coloring as they mature
34.childFriendlyNote: The acorns are getting brown caps like tiny hats. Each one has a baby oak tree inside, waiting for its chance!

34.description: Red-tailed hawks riding thermals over dry grasslands, molting into fresh flight feathers
34.childFriendlyNote: If you find a big striped feather on the ground, a hawk dropped it while growing a new one, nature's hand-me-downs!

34.description: Pelicans in post-breeding plumage, gathering in large roosting groups on piers and jetties
34.childFriendlyNote: Dozens of pelicans line up on the pier like they're waiting for a bus. They tuck their huge beaks into their feathers and nap!

34.description: Scrub-jays in fresh plumage after molt, intensely blue and active in gardens
34.childFriendlyNote: The scrub-jays look brand new. Their blue feathers are shiny and bright after growing in fresh, and they look proud of it.

35.description: Golden-brown hills stretching into early autumn, the dry season at its longest
35.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills have been this color for months, but don't worry, rain is coming! Just a few more weeks...

35.description: Valley oak acorns nearly ripe, first ones beginning to drop from branches
35.childFriendlyNote: Bonk. Acorns are starting to drop. Walk under an oak tree and hear them tap on the ground around you.

35.description: Ground squirrels collecting and caching acorns and seeds, preparing for autumn
35.childFriendlyNote: Squirrels are stuffing their cheeks so full of acorns they look like fuzzy balloons. They're saving snacks for later!

35.description: Green darner dragonflies beginning autumn migration, sometimes passing in visible streams
35.childFriendlyNote: The dragonflies are packing up for their trip south. Watch for groups of them all flying the same direction like tiny air traffic

35.description: Fence lizards still very active in late summer warmth, juveniles growing rapidly
35.childFriendlyNote: The baby lizards born in summer are growing fast. They do push-ups on the fence just like their parents taught them!

36.description: Hills still golden-brown, September often the hottest month in California
36.childFriendlyNote: Here is a surprise: September can be the hottest month here. The golden hills bake in the heat while other places are getting cooler.

36.description: Acorns dropping steadily, acorn woodpeckers and scrub-jays frantically collecting and storing them
36.childFriendlyNote: Acorns rain down from the oaks. Woodpeckers and jays race to grab them and hide them away. It's the Great Acorn Scramble!

36.description: Male tarantulas beginning their autumn mating walks, crossing roads and trails in search of females
36.childFriendlyNote: Big fuzzy spiders are going on walks! Male tarantulas wander around looking for a girlfriend. They're gentle and harmless, just say hello!

36.description: Red-tailed hawks soaring in September heat, hunting ground squirrels active at dawn
36.childFriendlyNote: The hawks circle over the golden hills in the warm September air. Listen for a long 'keeer'. Their cry echoes across the valley.

36.description: Acorn woodpeckers in overdrive, hammering acorns into granary trees, the tapping audible from far away
36.childFriendlyNote: Tap, tap, tap. The woodpeckers are stuffing acorns into every hole in their special tree. Some trees hold thousands of acorns.

37.description: Peak of tarantula mating season, males commonly seen walking across trails and roads in the evening
37.childFriendlyNote: It's tarantula time! These big gentle spiders walk slowly across paths looking for love. They have fuzzy legs and tiny eyes in a cluster

37.description: Hills still golden-brown in the September heat, but anticipation building for first autumn rains
37.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills are still here but the air feels different. Can you smell something? Rain might be coming soon...

37.description: First monarch butterflies arriving at California overwintering sites, trickling in from the north and east
37.childFriendlyNote: The first orange butterflies are coming back! They flew hundreds of miles to sleep in California's warm trees this winter

37.description: Acorns dropping heavily, the forest floor littered with brown nuts in their caps
37.childFriendlyNote: Walk under an oak and hear the crunch. Acorns are everywhere. Pick one up and pop the cap off, like a tiny hat.

37.description: Acorn woodpeckers working feverishly to fill every hole in their granary trees with fresh acorns
37.childFriendlyNote: The woodpeckers are busy, busy, busy. They fly back and forth with acorns in their beaks, tap them into holes, then zoom off for more.

38.description: Tarantula mating walks continuing, males wandering widely in late afternoon and evening
38.childFriendlyNote: More fuzzy spiders on the move. If you see one crossing a path, watch it carefully. It walks so slowly and carefully on its eight hairy legs!

38.description: Golden-brown hills in late September, the longest-dry landscapes starting to look tired
38.childFriendlyNote: The hills are still golden but they look thirsty. Everything is waiting for that first sip of autumn rain

38.description: More monarchs arriving at coastal overwintering groves, small clusters forming in eucalyptus and pines
38.childFriendlyNote: More orange butterflies arrive each day. They're finding their friends and starting to huddle together in the trees

38.description: Large quail coveys forming for autumn and winter, sometimes 30-40 birds gathering together
38.childFriendlyNote: Quail families are joining together into one big group. Sometimes 40 birds scurry across the path in a long wobbly line.

38.description: Scrub-jays intensely caching acorns, burying them in lawns and garden beds for winter retrieval
38.childFriendlyNote: Watch the blue jay bury an acorn, look around sneakily, then cover it with a leaf. It remembers thousands of hiding spots.

39.description: Tarantula mating season continuing, males still wandering trails on warm evenings
39.childFriendlyNote: The tarantula romance season is winding down. A few more big fuzzy spiders are still out looking for love

39.description: Monarch clusters growing at coastal overwintering sites, butterflies arriving steadily
39.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly tree is getting fuller! Orange wings flutter in, tired from their long journey, and join the sleepover

39.description: Acorn drop slowing, ground squirrels and jays have gathered most of the crop
39.childFriendlyNote: Most acorns have fallen and been scooped up by squirrels and birds. The oaks have given away their treasure

39.description: First autumn rain possible: 'the first flush' that brings dramatic greening of the golden hills within days
39.childFriendlyNote: Is that rain? The first rain after summer smells incredible, like the Earth sighing with relief. Watch for tiny green shoots in just a few days.

39.description: Red-tailed hawks continuing to hunt over dry grasslands, some migrant hawks arriving from the north
39.childFriendlyNote: More hawks are appearing. Visitor hawks from up north are joining our local ones for the winter!

40.description: First autumn rains awakening dormant seeds, green shoots appearing on golden hills within days of rainfall
40.childFriendlyNote: After months of gold, the first rain makes tiny green hairs sprout from the ground. The hills are waking up!

40.description: Monarch overwintering clusters growing steadily, dozens to hundreds gathering at traditional grove sites
40.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly sleepover is getting crowded. Hundreds of monarchs squeeze together on branches to stay warm at night!

40.description: Toyon berries beginning to ripen, clusters turning from green to orange-red on hillside shrubs
40.childFriendlyNote: Bush berries are starting to turn red like tiny Christmas ornaments. They'll be bright scarlet by December!

40.description: Large quail coveys foraging together through autumn days, huddling together at roost sites
40.childFriendlyNote: The quail gang sticks together. They eat together, sleep together, and run together. Safety in numbers!

40.description: Scrub-jays checking and re-caching stored acorns, moving them if they think another bird saw the hiding spot
40.childFriendlyNote: The blue jay digs up its hidden acorn, looks around suspiciously, and buries it somewhere new. It does not trust anyone.

41.description: Green flush spreading on hills after autumn rains, golden color giving way to fresh green on wetter slopes
41.childFriendlyNote: Green patches are spreading across the gold like someone is slowly coloring in the hills. The rain is bringing them back to life!

41.description: Monarch overwintering clusters well-established at Pacific Grove, Santa Cruz, and other coastal sites
41.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly trees look like they have orange leaves, but those are really thousands of butterflies huddled together.

41.description: Toyon berries turning redder, clusters becoming more conspicuous on hillside shrubs
41.childFriendlyNote: The berry bushes are getting redder every week. Birds are eyeing them hungrily but waiting until they're perfectly ripe!

41.description: First autumn mushrooms appearing after rains: chanterelles, porcini, and turkey tail pushing through damp soil and wood
41.childFriendlyNote: Rain and warm soil together make mushrooms. Weird and wonderful shapes pop up overnight on the forest floor, like magic. Look, but never eat a wild one.

41.description: Acorn woodpeckers guarding their granary trees fiercely, chattering at any bird that comes near
41.childFriendlyNote: The woodpeckers guard their acorn stash like tiny dragons protecting treasure, calling 'waka waka waka' if anyone gets too close.

42.description: Hills transitioning from gold to green as autumn rains continue, the famous California color change in reverse
42.childFriendlyNote: The golden hills are turning green again! It's backwards from other places. While leaves fall elsewhere, California's grass wakes up

42.description: Monarch clusters dense and settled, thousands of butterflies packed tightly on favored branches
42.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly tree is packed! When a cloud moves and sunshine hits, thousands of wings open at once. It's breathtaking!

42.description: Mushroom season building with continued rains, diverse species fruiting in woodlands and under oaks
42.childFriendlyNote: Mushrooms are popping up everywhere after the rain. Some look like umbrellas, some like shelves on trees, some like brain coral!

42.description: Toyon berries becoming bright red, attracting cedar waxwings and robins
42.childFriendlyNote: The toyon bushes are decked in red berries. This is the 'Christmas berry' that might be how Hollywood got its name!

42.description: First gray whales beginning their southbound migration from Alaska, early scouts passing the California coast
42.childFriendlyNote: The very first whales of the season are starting to swim south. Keep your eyes on the ocean for a misty spout!

43.description: Green rapidly spreading across hillsides with continued autumn rains, grass growing visibly day by day
43.childFriendlyNote: More green every day! The hills are like a coloring book being filled in with green crayon. Watch it spread after each rain

43.description: Monarch overwintering colonies at peak numbers, dense clusters hanging from coastal grove trees
43.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly trees are so full that the branches sag under the weight of thousands of sleeping monarchs.

43.description: Peak mushroom season, chanterelles golden in oak woodlands, amanitas bright under pines
43.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is a mushroom city! Golden trumpets, red-capped toadstools, and weird shapes you've never imagined. Nature is the best artist

43.description: Toyon berries brilliant scarlet, flocks of birds descending to feast
43.childFriendlyNote: Bright red berry bushes light up the hillsides. Noisy flocks of birds swoop in for the all-you-can-eat berry buffet!

43.description: Southbound gray whale migration building, more spouts visible from headlands and piers
43.childFriendlyNote: More whales are passing by each day. They're heading to warm water in Mexico to have their babies

44.description: Hills turning solidly green again as autumn rains establish, the seasonal transformation nearly complete
44.childFriendlyNote: The hills are green again. After months of gold, the rain has painted them fresh and bright. This is California's big costume change.

44.description: Monarch clusters large and stable at overwintering sites, butterflies basking on warm afternoons
44.childFriendlyNote: On sunny November afternoons, butterflies drift out from their cluster to sip nectar, then fly back to the cozy pile at night

44.description: Mushrooms flourishing in damp woodlands, new species appearing after each rain event
44.childFriendlyNote: Every time it rains, new mushrooms appear overnight. It's like a forest surprise party that happens again and again!

44.description: Southbound gray whale migration increasing, pregnant females leading the way to Baja lagoons
44.childFriendlyNote: More and more whale spouts puff up from the ocean. The mums-to-be are in a hurry to reach their warm nursery in Mexico

44.description: Toyon berries deep scarlet red, a festive sight on autumn hillsides
44.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas berry bushes look like they're already decorated for the holidays, bright red clusters everywhere!

45.description: Hills solidly green from autumn rains, fresh grass growing thick and soft
45.childFriendlyNote: The green hills are back for real. Sit in the soft new grass and feel how different it is from the scratchy golden stuff!

45.description: Monarch colonies settled for winter, clusters dense and beautiful at coastal grove sites
45.childFriendlyNote: The butterfly sleepover is in full swing. Thousands of monarchs cuddle on their favorite branches all winter long

45.description: Southbound gray whale migration well underway, regular sightings from coastal headlands
45.childFriendlyNote: Whale watching season is here. Grab your binoculars and scan the horizon from any high point near the ocean. Whoosh goes their misty breath.

45.description: Mushroom season strong, bracket fungi on dead wood, agarics in leaf litter, puffballs in grasslands
45.childFriendlyNote: Find a ripe puffball mushroom and tap it gently. A cloud of brown spore dust poofs out like nature's smoke bomb!

45.description: Pacific tree frogs becoming vocal again with autumn rains, calling from refilling ponds
45.childFriendlyNote: Ribbit, ribbit. The frogs are singing again. The rain filled up their ponds, and now they will not stop.

46.description: Hills lush green, winter rains building momentum and keeping grasslands fresh
46.childFriendlyNote: The green hills look like a fresh painting. Every time it rains, the colors get brighter and brighter

46.description: Monarch overwintering clusters stable, butterflies hanging motionless on cool days, active on warm ones
46.childFriendlyNote: On cold days the butterflies look like brown leaves. Then the sun comes out and they open their wings to show off their orange!

46.description: Peak of early southbound migration, whales spouting regularly along the coastline
46.childFriendlyNote: The whale highway is busy! These giant travelers swim day and night, resting by floating at the surface

46.description: Mushroom season continuing strong, new flushes appearing after each rain
46.childFriendlyNote: After every rain, check under the trees for new mushrooms. They pop up overnight like the forest is playing peek-a-boo!

46.description: Toyon berries at their most vibrant red, a splash of festive color in the green hillsides
46.childFriendlyNote: Red berries glow against the green hills like nature put up its own holiday decorations, no lights needed!

46.description: Tree frogs calling more regularly from rain-fed ponds, the evening chorus building
46.childFriendlyNote: The frog choir is warming up. Every evening a few more voices join in until the whole pond is singing!

47.description: Hillsides richly green, the wet season well established and grass growing vigorously
47.childFriendlyNote: The hills smell fresh and earthy after rain. Lean down and breathe in that wonderful green smell

47.description: Monarch clusters holding through November, an essential overwintering habitat for western population
47.childFriendlyNote: The butterflies will stay cuddled in their trees all winter. They barely eat, just sip a little water on warm days

47.description: Southbound whale migration steady, mothers-to-be passing closest to shore
47.childFriendlyNote: Pregnant whale mums swim close to the coast where the water is calmer. They need to save energy for the long trip!

47.description: Mushroom diversity at its highest, mycologists foraging for chanterelles and black trumpets
47.childFriendlyNote: Golden trumpets, tiny parasols, brain-shaped blobs. The mushroom parade has every shape you can imagine hiding under the trees.

47.description: Anna's hummingbirds beginning courtship, males performing dive displays, one of the earliest nesting birds
47.childFriendlyNote: While other birds rest for winter, the tiny hummingbird is already flirting. He flies up high, then zooms down making a loud chirp.

48.description: Green hills in late November, the rainy season well established and grass thick and lush
48.childFriendlyNote: The hills are deep green and soft. Lie down on them and look up at the puffy rain clouds rolling by

48.description: Monarch overwintering colonies well settled, protected groves essential for survival
48.childFriendlyNote: The butterflies are snuggled in for the winter. Visit a butterfly grove and see thousands hanging together. Whisper, so you don't wake them!

48.description: Southbound gray whale migration in full flow, daily sightings from whale-watching points
48.childFriendlyNote: The whale parade is going strong. On a good day you might count ten or more misty spouts from one headland!

48.description: Toyon berries still bright red, robins and cedar waxwings feasting on the abundant fruit
48.childFriendlyNote: Masked cedar waxwing birds with yellow-tipped tails swarm the berry bushes. They pass berries to each other beak-to-beak. So polite!

48.description: Anna's hummingbirds establishing territories, males singing their scratchy buzzing song from prominent perches
48.childFriendlyNote: The hummingbird sits on a high branch and makes a scratchy, buzzy song. He's the tiniest bird with the biggest attitude!

49.description: Hills vividly green in early December, winter rains keeping the landscape lush
49.childFriendlyNote: While other places get snow, California's hills are their greenest. It's our own special kind of winter wonderland!

49.description: Monarch overwintering clusters dense and quiet, butterflies barely moving on cold December days
49.childFriendlyNote: The butterflies are so still they look like dried leaves hanging from branches, but wait for sunshine and watch them come alive!

49.description: Southbound gray whale migration at peak, highest daily counts of whales passing the coast
49.childFriendlyNote: December is the best month for whale watching. More whales pass by now than at any other time. Grab hot cocoa and your binoculars.

49.description: Toyon berries still blazing red on hillsides, the original 'Christmas berry' of California
49.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas berry is ready for Christmas! Bright red clusters decorate the green hillsides like nature's own holiday display

49.description: Anna's hummingbirds actively courting, some females already building nests despite the short days
49.childFriendlyNote: While other birds wait for spring, the amazing hummingbird is already making a nest! She builds it from spider silk and plant fluff. It stretches as the babies grow

49.description: Mushroom season strong through December, wet woodlands producing abundant fruiting bodies
49.childFriendlyNote: The forest floor is still full of mushroom surprises after every rain. Each walk reveals something new and strange and wonderful

50.description: Hills bright green in mid-December, the wet season at full strength
50.childFriendlyNote: The green hills glow in the winter light. Rain keeps them soft and bright like a giant green blanket

50.description: Monarch overwintering clusters at midwinter, butterflies conserving energy in dense groups
50.childFriendlyNote: The butterflies are at their coziest. Packed tight together for warmth, they'll stay like this until the days get longer

50.description: Southbound gray whale migration continuing, steady procession visible from shore
50.childFriendlyNote: Whales are still streaming south. They swim about 5 miles per hour, which is slower than you can ride a bike!

50.description: Anna's hummingbirds nesting in December, some already incubating eggs in tiny lichen-covered nests
50.childFriendlyNote: Believe it or not, some hummingbirds are sitting on eggs right now, in December. The nest is so tiny you would walk right past it.

50.description: Pacific tree frogs calling from rain-filled ponds and ditches, winter breeding season beginning
50.childFriendlyNote: Ribbit, ribbit from every puddle. The tiny green frogs start their winter singing as the rains fill up their ponds.

51.description: Green hillsides in late December, a stark contrast to the snow-covered landscapes of other US regions
51.childFriendlyNote: While kids in other states build snowmen, California kids play on bright green hills, two kinds of winter wonderland!

51.description: Monarch overwintering clusters at deep winter state, butterflies barely moving, conserving every calorie
51.childFriendlyNote: The butterflies are fast asleep in their tree, folded up so tight they look like brown leaves. Shhh!

51.description: Southbound gray whale migration strong, some early mothers already in Baja lagoons with newborn calves
51.childFriendlyNote: The whales keep swimming south past our coast. Some mums have already reached Mexico and are cuddling their brand new babies!

51.description: Toyon berries still red and festive, some being eaten by cedar waxwings and mockingbirds
51.childFriendlyNote: The Christmas berries are perfect for the holidays. Birds have been nibbling but there are still plenty of red clusters to enjoy

51.description: Anna's hummingbirds incubating or feeding tiny chicks, remarkably early nesters even in late December
51.childFriendlyNote: Some hummingbird babies are already hatching. They are the size of a coffee bean, and mum keeps them warm with her tiny body.

52.description: Hills green and lush at year's end, winter rains sustaining the verdant landscape into the new year
52.childFriendlyNote: The year ends with bright green hills. The rain has been feeding the grass for weeks, and it looks alive and fresh.

52.description: Monarch overwintering clusters holding steady through the shortest days of winter
52.childFriendlyNote: Thousands of butterflies end the year together in their cozy tree, the biggest sleepover in the animal kingdom!

52.description: Southbound gray whale migration in full swing as the year turns, a living river of whales along the coast
52.childFriendlyNote: As the year ends, whales are still swimming past. They have been making this same trip for millions of years. Happy New Year, whales.

52.description: Anna's hummingbirds continuing their winter breeding cycle, dive displays and feeding on winter flowers
52.childFriendlyNote: The sparkly hummingbird doesn't care that it's winter. He's diving and squeaking and showing off just like it's spring!

52.description: Pacific tree frogs chorusing on rainy evenings, their ribbit the soundtrack of California's wet season
52.childFriendlyNote: The year ends with a frog concert. Step outside on a rainy evening and hear hundreds of tiny frogs singing 'ribbit, ribbit' into the new year.

52.description: Mushroom season going strong, winter rains keeping the forest floor damp and productive
52.childFriendlyNote: Mushrooms are still popping up like little umbrellas in the wet forest, a perfect treasure hunt for the last days of the year!
